checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split numerals from their immediately following unit/date/measure, breaking single referents and causing high contradiction/cohesion loss.
checks.evidence: cmn_hans_cn_712, cmn_hans_cn_1129, cmn_hans_cn_1169, cmn_hans_cn_132, cmn_hans_cn_324 — each case shows a marker separating an Arabic numeral from its following unit (years, scores, measures, counts) that the target keeps together.
checks.type_predicate: Applies when a marker sits between an Arabic numeral (one or more digits) and the immediately following unit or temporal/measure character (a contiguous numeral+unit token such as a year, date, score, or quantity).

edit.text: Do not cut between an Arabic numeral and its immediately following unit/temporal character; keep digits and their unit together (years, dates, scores, measures).

orders.diagnosis: When two candidate cuts fall inside the same nominal modifier, the prompt sometimes prefers an earlier internal split; the measured targets prefer the later cut that preserves the modifier+head span.
orders.evidence: cmn_hans_cn_712, cmn_hans_cn_324, cmn_hans_cn_1169 — in each sentence the target prefers the later marker that keeps a multi-character modifier attached to its head, while the prompt favored an earlier internal split.
orders.type_predicate: Applies when both candidate markers occur within the same multi-character nominal modifier and one marker lies inside that modifier while the other lies immediately after it (so the latter would keep modifier+head together).

edit.text: When one marker is inside a nominal modifier and another immediately follows that modifier, prefer the latter marker that keeps modifier+head together.
